dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Hi, yeah, hi. I'm calling about water in the street, it's, um, it's been sitting there since the storm and nobody's done anything. I mean the nor'easter, last weekend, Saturday into Sunday.
Okay, sorry to hear that. Let me grab some details. Where's the water, what's it doing?

It's over the curb. It's across the whole sidewalk, like you can't walk there. And it keeps happening, every time we get a real rain the drain just doesn't take it, and then somebody's got to call and, and, hold on. Hey, not now, I'm on the phone. Sorry. Go ahead.
No worries, take your time. So water over the curb and across the sidewalk. Is it a storm drain nearby that looks clogged, or is it more like the whole low spot is holding water?

Both, honestly. The drain's right there and it's packed with leaves and junk, and the water just pools. And a delivery truck got stuck in it this morning. Like, actually stuck, the driver was out there for a good while before he got it moving. Which, I mean, if a truck can't get through, what are we...
Yeah, that's not great. Got it, truck stuck in the standing water this morning. Writing that down.

And the sidewalk, it's a sheet of mud and grit. Everything the water brought down just got left there. It's all slick. I've got kids walking to the bus and they're trying to go around it into the road. Colin, I said hang on. Sorry.

That's all right. So mud and grit coating the sidewalk, kids having to step out around it. That's a safety thing, I'll make sure that's noted. Is the water still standing there right now, or has it gone down some?

Gone down a little but it's still there. It's, it's a puddle the size of, I don't know, half the lane. I called about this kind of thing before, a different time, and I feel like it just goes in a pile somewhere. Nobody came.
I hear you. I can't see that earlier call from here without a location, though. Can you tell me the cross streets or the nearest landmark, so the crew knows which drain?

Yeah, so, um. Hang on, I'm trying to think how to say it. It's, ugh, my phone, I'm walking around and the screen's, wait, that's my e-reader, I grabbed the wrong thing. It's got a cracked screen from when it fell, but it still works, so I keep using it. Anyway. Sorry. You were asking about the location.
No problem. Happens. Cross streets or a landmark is what I'm after.
Right. I'd rather not say the address on this line, my kid's right here. Can you just put it in as the drain by the school bus stop on my block, and I'll, um, I can give it when you call back?
Sure, I can note it that way, but the crew will need the actual spot to find it. When I call you back we can get the exact location. What's a good number?
It's 401-555-0189. That's my cell.
Okay, 401-555-0189. I'll put in a request to clear the drain and look at the sidewalk, and mark it as urgent because of the truck and the kids. I'll have someone from our side call you.
Okay. Yeah. Can you, like, call me back when it's done? Not just when you get the request in. When somebody has actually been out there.
Yep, I'll flag it for a call back once the crew has been out. Might take a day or two, they've been slammed since the weekend with the storm.
Sure, I get that. I just, it's the same thing every time. Okay. Thank you. Colin, put that down! Sorry. Thanks, Kevin.
No problem, David. Take care, and keep the kids out of that water.
